title: Ending a Tasmanian tenancy
description: Steps for an owner ending a lease in Tasmania. Summarised from Consumer Affairs Tasmania guidance on owners ending a lease and on bonds.

items.title: Confirm you have a listed ground to end the lease
For a fixed term ending, serve the Tasmanian notice to vacate 42 to 60 days before the end date
For a non-fixed term, give 42 days' notice for sale, renovation, family use or non-rental use (60 days for a lender's sale)
For a sale, attach proof of the agreement to sell
For a breach or rent arrears, allow 14 days for the tenant to fix it
Include the date, names, property, reason and the date vacant possession is due
Count clear days and avoid an end date on a public holiday
Serve it in person, at the tenant's address or by a process server, ideally with a witness
If the tenant stays, apply to the Magistrates Court within 28 days of the notice taking effect
Inspect against the ingoing condition report
Claim the bond through Tasmanian MyBond; the tenant can approve or dispute it
